definition.def: An abrupt change or action is very sudden, often in a way which is unpleasant.
examples: Rosie's idyllic world came to an abrupt end when her parents' marriage broke up.
The recession brought an abrupt halt to this happiness.
His abrupt departure is bound to raise questions.

definition.def: Someone who is abrupt speaks in a rather rude, unfriendly way.
examples: He was abrupt to the point of rudeness.
Cross was a little taken aback by her abrupt manner.

examples.sentence: "But we have observed that there was an abrupt change about 4,100 years ago, when the amount of evaporation from the lake exceeded the rainfall - indicative of a drought."
These abrupt changes will produce either positive or negative feelings.

"With the eaves extending out on all sides like balancing poles," says Mr Ishida, "the building responds to even the most powerful jolt of an earthquake with a graceful swaying, never an abrupt shaking."
